text: Verification codes sync across all your devices when you sign in to your Google Account
quote: With Google Authenticator, you can synchronize your verification codes across all your devices, simply by signing in to your Google Account.

text: Signing in on a new device automatically syncs your codes to it, so you are not locked out when you change devices
quote: When you sign in to your Google Account within Google Authenticator on a new device, your codes are automatically synced to this device.

text: The app can be used without signing in to any account
quote: When you first open the app, tap Use without an account.

text: Codes can be moved manually to a new device by generating a QR code on the old device and scanning it on the new one, even without a Google Account
quote: On your old device, create a QR code... On your new device, tap Scan QR code

text: Codes for multiple Google Accounts can be synced and shown together on the same mobile device
quote: Authenticator can sync codes for multiple Google Accounts and display them from the same mobile device.

text: You can edit a code's username or change which Google Account it is saved to
quote: To edit your Authenticator code on Android, swipe left on any code to show the edit option. You can update the username for the code or change the associated Google Account where that code is saved.

text: Codes can be reordered by touching, holding, and dragging them
quote: To organize your Authenticator codes, touch and hold any code, then drag to reorder to a desired location.

text: Codes can be searched by entering text that matches the username
quote: To search through your Google Authenticator codes, enter any text matching the username to find the code.

text: Individual codes can be deleted by swiping on them
quote: To delete an Authenticator code on Android, swipe right on any code to show the delete option.

text: Privacy Screen requires a device PIN, pattern, or biometric check before the app can be used
quote: For additional protection, you can turn on Privacy Screen in Google Authenticator. This requires a verification from your device, like a PIN, pattern or biometric prompt, before the app can be used.

text: Codes can be generated without an internet connection or mobile service
quote: You can still generate codes without an internet connection or mobile service.

text: Supports the HOTP (RFC 4226) and TOTP (RFC 6238) one-time password algorithms
quote: These implementations support the HMAC-Based One-time Password (HOTP) algorithm specified in RFC 4226 and the Time-based One-time Password (TOTP) algorithm specified in RFC 6238.

text: A public GitHub project includes one-time passcode generator implementations for several mobile platforms
quote: The Google Authenticator project includes implementations of one-time passcode generators for several mobile platforms.

text: Provides a Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) for using one-time passcodes with system logins
Generates one-time verification codes for any site or app that supports authenticator-app 2-Step Verification
quote: The Google Authenticator app can generate one-time verification codes for sites and apps that support Authenticator app 2-Step Verification.

text: Can generate codes to sign in to your Google Account with 2-Step Verification
quote: If you set up 2-Step Verification, you can use the Google Authenticator app to generate codes to sign in to your Google Account.

text: Google encrypts Authenticator codes both in transit and at rest
quote: Google encrypts Authenticator codes both in transit and at rest across our products.

text: Synced codes can be removed from a device by removing that device from your Google Account
quote: If your codes are synced to your Google Account, you can remove codes by [removing the device from your Google Account](/accounts/answer/3067630#remove).
